transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Security), Samuel Reed (CISO, Pinecrest), Aisha Khan (Head Cloud), Tom Hsu (Network Arch), Maya Ortiz (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick security deep dive focused on Private VPC/on-prem deployment model, network isolation, ingress/egress controls, firewalling, and compliance evidence (SOC2/ISO). Customer wants to validate architecture for regulated finance workloads and confirm encryption/KMS, audit logs, and RBAC/SSO posture.

Topics:
- VPC isolation (subnets, private link, transit gateway)
- Ingress/egress patterns and firewalling (NGFW, security groups, NACLs)
- Private deployment options (VPC-hosted control plane vs on-prem air-gapped)
- Identity and access (SSO, SAML, RBAC)
- Audit logs, SIEM integration, and retention for compliance
- Encryption-at-rest/network (KMS/HSM) and data residency

Transcript:
00:00:05 Laura Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'll hand over to Marcus to run through the architecture then Priya will cover compliance artifacts.
00:00:12 Marcus Diaz: Hey all, quick agenda. We'll sketch the VPC layout, how we handle ingress and egress, firewall rules, and then talk about KMS and logging. Please interrupt, I know there's lots of stakeholders.
00:00:28 Samuel Reed: Good, we mainly want to know if Redwood can operate fully in our VPC and meet our egress restrictions and audit retention. Also SOC 2 artifacts.
00:00:38 Marcus Diaz: Absolutely. At a high level Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC with a customer-managed control plane — that gives you network isolation, and the compute nodes sit in private subnets. For on-prem we do an air-gapped bundle but today we'll focus VPC-first.
00:00:58 Aisha Khan: When you say "customer-managed control plane" do you mean we run the API endpoint inside our VPC, or is there a shared endpoint that crosses networks?
00:01:07 Marcus Diaz: Good question. We support two patterns: 1) Local control plane — endpoints and management inside your VPC, so traffic never leaves your environment except what you allow. 2) Hosted control plane with private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink or Transit Gateway) — management plane traffic goes over a PrivateLink endpoint. Both options keep data plane inside your subnets.
00:01:29 Tom Hsu: For PrivateLink we need to know IP ranges and whether you use NAT for egress; our security team requires egress via approved NATs.
00:01:36 Marcus Diaz: We provide CIDR ranges for the interface endpoints; for egress we support routing through your NAT gateways or firewall appliances. We don't force outbound traffic to public internet unless you enable model pulls for hosted model updates.
00:01:51 Maya Ortiz: What about firewalling — do you expect us to open up ports to the world for health checks or anything?
00:01:56 Marcus Diaz: No, health checks are internal. For traffic we recommend restricting load balancers to internal-only, use an internal ALB/NLB. Management plane can be restricted to specific admin IPs or over PrivateLink.
00:02:10 Priya Patel: Also, we recommend RBAC at both infra and app level. Redwood integrates with SAML/SSO for identity — you map AD groups to roles. We also support SCIM for provisioning. There is a local admin role that can be disabled if you want full SSO lockout.
00:02:27 Samuel Reed: SCIM is important for us. Can you tie into our Okta and push group changes automatically?
00:02:31 Priya Patel: Yes, Okta + SAML + SCIM works. We have a sample SSO config in the doc we will share. Some customers keep a break-glass account for emergencies.
00:02:42 Tom Hsu: On network isolation, do your nodes require outbound internet to download docker images or model artifacts? We have a rule against outbound to arbitrary endpoints.
00:02:51 Marcus Diaz: For Private deployments you can preload images — we provide an offline bundle for on-prem. For VPC deployments, images can be pulled from our artifact repo via your NAT or via a customer-provided object store (S3) if you want complete control. We can also support a VPC endpoint to our S3 mirror.
00:03:10 Aisha Khan: Ok so we could mirror artifacts to our S3 and block direct internet. Good.
00:03:16 Maya Ortiz: Audit logs and retention — what do you ship and can we forward to our SIEM?
00:03:22 Priya Patel: Audit logs include user actions, API calls, model version rollouts, and system alerts. We forward logs to your CloudWatch/Log Analytics/Splunk via Kinesis/forwarder. Retention is configurable — we can keep 90/365/indef based on contracts. For compliance we can provide immutable export and attestations.
00:03:42 Samuel Reed: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need chain-of-custody proof for certain incidents.
00:03:48 Priya Patel: We support log signing for longer-term retention and can integrate with your WORM storage. For the on-prem bundle, logs can be written to customer-managed HSM-backed storage.
00:03:59 Marcus Diaz: Network controls we typically recommend: private subnets for compute, no public IPs, security groups with least privilege, NACLs as defense-in-depth, and an NGFW in the egress path to control destinations. If you use Transit Gateway we can attach to a dedicated routing table.
00:04:18 Tom Hsu: How do you handle egress filtering for model telemetry — do you send metrics back to Redwood?
00:04:24 Marcus Diaz: By default telemetry is optional. For Private we disable outbound telemetry unless you enable it. For hosted we collect metrics; in Private we can direct metrics to your Prometheus or push through our forwarder to your telemetry pipeline.
00:04:36 Aisha Khan: Encryption — keys at rest and in transit? KMS? HSM?
00:04:40 Priya Patel: Data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS keys (we integrate with AWS KMS). For higher assurance you can use an external HSM or Cloud HSM and we support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). In-transit TLS is enforced with mutual TLS for control plane connections, and mTLS is available for node-to-node in the cluster.
00:05:00 Samuel Reed: We require customer-held keys and no Redwood access to plaintext. Is that supported?
00:05:05 Priya Patel: Yes — with BYOK and encrypted KV for secrets, Redwood cannot decrypt artifacts without the key. There's an optional key escrow pattern but the default is customer-only key access.
00:05:14 Tom Hsu: For on-prem, how is networking handled for multi-rack deployments? Do you recommend an edge firewall and internal overlay?
00:05:21 Marcus Diaz: For on-prem we typically recommend an internal overlay network (calico/ovn) with tenant isolation and an edge NGFW for north-south. We also support hardware load balancers in front and use IPsec for any connectivity back to cloud services.
00:05:35 Maya Ortiz: Regarding SOC 2 and ISO, what artifacts can you provide to our auditors?
00:05:39 Priya Patel: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 attestation, policy docs, encryption key handling procedures, incident response runbooks, and pen test summaries. For deeper dives we do red team summaries and remediation reports.
00:05:52 Samuel Reed: Great.
00:05:55 Laura Chen: I'll drop links after the call. Marcus, can you speak to firewall rule templates?
00:06:00 Marcus Diaz: Sure. Typical pattern: allow inbound from specific admin IPs to management control plane over mTLS ports, allow internal subnets for node communication on ports X,Y, deny all outbound except to approved artifact mirrors and telemetry endpoints. We'll include a CSV template with ports and CIDRs.
00:06:17 Tom Hsu: How about DNS — do you require any split-horizon?
00:06:20 Marcus Diaz: We recommend internal DNS entries for control plane endpoints and optional split-horizon so public DNS doesn't resolve internal endpoints. For PrivateLink you can configure private hosted zones.
00:06:29 Aisha Khan: Any guidance on ephemeral credentials and token lifetimes?
00:06:33 Priya Patel: Tokens are short lived by default, refreshable via your SSO. We recommend very short TTLs for admin tokens and enable session revocation on SCIM group changes.
00:06:44 Samuel Reed: If we need FIPS-validated TLS or FIPS level crypto for keys, is that supported?
00:06:49 Priya Patel: We can run on FIPS-mode OS images and use Cloud HSM or HSM appliances for key material, yes. We'll need to coordinate validation scope with your compliance team.
00:06:59 Marcus Diaz: Quick note on monitoring: we emit metrics for latency, token counts, and model throughput. Logs include correlation IDs so you can trace a request through the infra for audits.
00:07:12 Tom Hsu: For network ACLs vs security groups: which do you prefer?
00:07:15 Marcus Diaz: Security groups for stateful controls, NACLs for subnet level explicit deny rules as second layer. We don't rely solely on NACLs.
00:07:24 Maya Ortiz: If we sign an NDA / proceed to pilot, what's the timeline for SOC artifacts?
00:07:29 Priya Patel: We can share SOC 2 and ISO summary within 48 hours after an NDA is in place, and full artifacts under an auditor NDA.
00:07:37 Aisha Khan: We have a requirement for egress whitelisting — you mentioned you can supply a static list of IPs?
00:07:43 Marcus Diaz: For PrivateLink you get interface endpoints, no public IPs; for any outbound we can supply the egress IP ranges for our managed services, or you can route through your own proxies. We'll produce an egress CIDR list.
00:07:59 Samuel Reed: One more — how do you handle model updates and version rollback in a secure way?
00:08:04 Marcus Diaz: Model artifacts are versioned and checksummed. For Private we can sign artifacts and you can verify signatures before deployment. Rollbacks are orchestrated via the control plane and require RBAC approvals; audit trails record who initiated rollouts.
00:08:19 Tom Hsu: Is there a hard dependency on external DNS or cloud IAM for the core runtime?
00:08:24 Marcus Diaz: No hard dependency. You can run the runtime fully with local service accounts and local DNS if desired for air-gapped setups. The only external dependency is optional artifact/metrics endpoints if you want them.
00:08:36 Maya Ortiz: This is helpful. Recap and next steps?
00:08:40 Laura Chen: Recap: Redwood to share VPC diagram, SOC2/ISO artifacts, firewall template, and schedule on-prem workshop. Pinecrest to share egress whitelist and current NAT architecture.
00:08:52 Samuel Reed: Correct. Also please include sample SSO/SCIM config.
00:08:58 Priya Patel: Will do. I'll attach the sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping for Okta.
00:09:03 Marcus Diaz: I'll put together the VPC diagram and include details for Transit Gateway attachments, PrivateLink endpoints, firewall appliance placement, and NACL/security group examples. Link to diagram will be posted in the follow-up.
00:09:16 Aisha Khan: Thanks, and please include the option for BYOK and Cloud HSM notes.
00:09:20 Priya Patel: Yep.
00:09:22 Laura Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and set the workshop.
00:09:26 Samuel Reed: Thanks all.

Call recap (verbatim):
- Redwood Private can be fully deployed inside Pinecrest VPC or on-prem air-gapped bundle.
- Identity integrations: SAML/SSO + SCIM; RBAC mapping supported; break-glass patterns available.
- Network controls: private subnets, no public IPs, internal ALB/NLB, NGFW in egress path, security groups + NACLs.
- Egress: can route through customer NATs/proxies; Redwood can provide egress CIDR list or use PrivateLink.
- Logging: Audit logs, signed logs, SIEM forwarding supported; retention configurable for compliance.
- Encryption: Customer-managed KMS, BYOK, HSM support, mTLS for control plane; option for FIPS-mode.
